# Focus Spoofer

> Free Chrome extension (Manifest V3) that stops websites from detecting tab switches, minimizing or using another window, on the tabs you choose.

Key facts:

- Price: free. No account. Current version: 1.8.
- Browsers: Chrome, Brave and Microsoft Edge on Windows, macOS, Linux and ChromeOS. Not Firefox or Safari.
- What it does: keeps `document.hidden` false and `document.visibilityState` "visible"; blocks `visibilitychange`, `pagehide` and window-level `blur`/`mouseleave`; keeps `document.hasFocus()` true; keeps `requestAnimationFrame` and `requestVideoFrameCallback` firing in hidden tabs; optionally randomizes canvas, WebGL and audio fingerprints (on by default, can be turned off).
- Scope: only on tabs the user turns it on for, or on sites marked "Always protect". Element-level focus, blur and hover events inside the page keep working.
- What it does not do: it does not get around exam proctoring or anti-cheat software, and it cannot run on chrome:// pages, the Chrome Web Store or the built-in PDF viewer.
- Privacy: browsing history, visited sites and page content never leave the browser. Optional anonymous daily usage counts with no identifier are off by default.

## Pages

- [Focus Spoofer](https://focus.oddworks.us/): What the extension does, the three ways a tab gives you away and how it hides them, and an FAQ.
- [Tab-switch detection test](https://focus.oddworks.us/test): Live page that shows whether it can detect you switching tabs or fingerprint your canvas.
- [Privacy policy](https://focus.oddworks.us/privacy): Exactly what is and isn't collected.
